predecessors.name: State of East Indonesia
predecessors.text: 'the islands of Ambon, Buru, and Seram, which currently make up most of the province of Maluku'; Natural Earth's Maluku (which also holds the south-eastern islands) stands for the claim

successors.name: Republic of Indonesia
successors.text: Seram (Ceram), 17,100 km2, where 'the RMS government went to Ceram in December' 1950 and the guerrilla war went on (a 75 km circle)

ledger.x: 1950: the Republic of South Maluku is proclaimed at Ambon on 25 April by demobilised ex-KNIL soldiers and others, claiming 'the islands of Ambon, Buru, and Seram'.
1950: Ambon falls on 5 November: 'the city of Ambon fell to APRIS'.
1950: the RMS government moves from Ambon to Ceram in December.
1963: the Republic of South Maluku ceases to hold land; its government-in-exile moved to the Netherlands in 1966.

wars.name: South Maluku rebellion
wars.outcome: APRIS invaded Ambon on 28 September 1950 and took the city on 5 November; the RMS government fought on in Ceram until 1962-1963.

certainty.note: A claim over three islands and then a guerrilla refuge; only Ambon's fall is a dated place.
